correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every degree-at-most-four constant 3-order-width support to modes 0, 2 and 4 after translation, uses the exact area identity, converts convexity to a nonnegative degree-two trigonometric polynomial, and gives a self-contained Fejer--Riesz root-pairing argument. With factor magnitudes x,y,z, the exact deficit objective is bounded by 4[y^2(x+z)^2/3+x^2z^2/15]. At fixed s=x^2+z^2 it is increasing in q=xz, forcing x=z; the remaining quadratic has unique maximum u=10/39 and value 80/117. The displayed support has curvature density equal to a nonnegative perfect square and attains the bound. The bundled checker independently replays the algebraic identities but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The result is a complete sharp solution of the first nontrivial two-harmonic Fourier cutoff of a published generalized Blaschke--Lebesgue least-area problem. It supplies an exact minimum, an explicit extremal support, and a reusable conversion of convexity to a degree-two Fejer--Riesz optimization. This is structurally more informative than a numerical truncation or a one-parameter perturbation, while being explicit about not resolving the unrestricted problem.
